problem: Existing socially-aware navigation methods either predict pedestrian motion (causing detours/collisions) or issue one-way alerts (beeps, nudges) that are ambiguous, intrusive and cannot take in pedestrian intent, so there is no true bidirectional human-robot interaction.
motivation: Service robots in shared spaces (e.g. airports) need to negotiate right-of-way naturally. One-way signals cannot resolve ambiguity, while natural language lets the robot understand pedestrian requests and explain its own intent. This requires jointly controlling continuous velocity and discrete interaction decisions.
key_idea: Combine a Hybrid Soft Actor-Critic (continuous velocities + discrete interaction codes) with an LLM (GPT-4) that turns the discrete action into spoken language, and with a language encoder that feeds pedestrian speech back into the policy state.
insight: Two-way language interaction reduces collisions relative to a one-way-warning-only variant: removing the LLM module (HSAC) raises Square collision from 0.08 to 0.14 and Crosswalk from 0.09 to 0.13. A richer 4-D discrete action space (none/stop/margin-right/margin-left) beats a 2-D one (Crosswalk success 0.87 to 0.91). The gains come mostly from communication resolving ambiguity rather than from detouring. Caveat: the evaluation is a single scripted pedestrian in a 2D simulator, and the baselines are not designed for interaction.
method: Img_PreNet: 3 conv + 3 maxpool layers over the 180° laser-scan grid and 3-channel pedestrian grid map, giving a 512-d state S_i (following Yao et al. 2021)
Lang_PreNet: encodes the pedestrian's/robot's voice messages during a potential collision into a condition vector S_c
State_PreNet: concatenates S_i, the 9-d relative goal position S_p and S_c, and passes them through an FC layer to a 512-d state

HSAC module: actor with shared hidden state producing a discrete distribution over interaction codes and a Gaussian for [v, ω]=tanh(μ+εσ); critic takes the state and continuous action and outputs Q-values for all discrete actions
Lang_GenNet: GPT-4 converts the discrete action code (none/stop/margin-right/margin-left) into natural-language speech to the pedestrian
Reward: goal (arrive/near-miss penalty/collision), shaping, step penalty, plus an interaction reward for requests or responses aligned with the pedestrian trajectory

setting.backbone: HSAC (CNN PreNets + actor-critic, trained from scratch) + GPT-4 (frozen) for utterance generation
setting.training_data: Trained by RL for 128,000 steps in a 2D OpenCV simulator with IRVO-controlled pedestrians; no extra data
setting.observation: 2D LiDAR scan grid map, pedestrian position/speed grid map, relative goal pose over 3 steps, and voice messages
setting.action_space: hybrid: continuous linear velocity [0,0.6] m/s and angular velocity [-0.9,0.9] rad/s, plus discrete interaction code (none, stop, margin-right, margin-left)
setting.simulator: custom 2D OpenCV simulator; Gazebo; real world
setting.privileged: none stated (Gazebo uses leg tracking for pedestrian speed)

numbers_note: Only custom 2D-simulator results are quantitative; Gazebo and real-world results are qualitative. Training time is printed without units. Success/collision values also carry ± std in the paper (e.g. Square 0.91 ± 0.022).
results: In three 2D-simulator scenes HSAC-LLM reaches success 0.91/0.93/0.91 and collision 0.08/0.07/0.09, beating A2C, PPO and TD3 (strongest baseline TD3: 0.85/0.77/0.85 success). It also uses the fewest steps. Qualitative Gazebo and real JetAuto Pro hallway demos show it working with only a 2D LiDAR.
limitations: Quantitative evaluation is only in a custom 2D simulator with a single scripted (IRVO) pedestrian; Gazebo and real-world results are qualitative demos
Baselines are non-interactive DRL methods; there is no comparison to other interaction methods (beeping) or other LLM-based approaches, and the discrete action set is small and fixed
Lang_PreNet is under-specified and GPT-4 only verbalizes the discrete action, so the LLM's actual role in decision-making is limited; latency and multi-pedestrian scenarios are not evaluated
builds_on: Soft Actor-Critic for discrete/hybrid actions (Delalleau et al.)
CrowdNav-style DRL with Img_PreNet (Yao et al. 2021)
